1.title: Marl-Limestone: Alsace's Largest Geological Family
1.html: Marl-limestone (marno-calcaires) is the largest of the ten families, with 13 Grand Crus — formed by alternating Oligocene conglomerate and marl, with a texture slightly richer than pure limestone and the dual advantages of water retention and drainage, an important stage for Gewurztraminer to show structure and power. This lesson first covers 7 of the sites.
2.title: Marl-Limestone Group (Part 1a)
2.items.0.label: Altenberg de Wolxheim (Wolxheim, 31.20 ha)
2.items.0.desc: Lias plus Dogger marl-limestone, stony. Recorded by medieval church institutions including the Bishop of Strasbourg (1003) and Hohenbourg abbey (1188). Napoleon I is said to have praised its Riesling. Riesling (18 ha) + Gewurztraminer (8 ha), powerful, harmonious and delicate in flavour.
2.items.1.label: Eichberg (Eguisheim, 57.62 ha)
2.items.1.desc: Oligocene conglomerate marl, in the area with the lowest rainfall around Colmar. Tax records from Marbach abbey in the 11th century. Riesling, Gewurztraminer and Pinot Gris; the wines are extremely rich, with delicate flavour and prominent fruit, and excellent ageing potential.
2.items.2.label: Florimont (Ingersheim & Katzenthal, 21 ha)
2.items.2.desc: Bathonian / Bajocian limestone plus Oligocene conglomerate marl, in the "Colmar ellipse" with only about 550 mm of rain a year. Gewurztraminer is the leading variety, with excellent Riesling too. Full, balanced wines with great ageing potential.
2.items.3.label: Goldert (Gueberschwihr, 45.35 ha)
2.items.3.desc: Dogger oolitic limestone plus Quaternary dissolution deposits. A well-known wine village as early as 750. In 1728 the city council of Lucerne granted its wines priority selling positions in the market. Gewurztraminer is the first choice, showing golden colour and excellent harmony, the name coming from "gold" (Gold).
3.title: Marl-Limestone Group (Part 1b)
3.items.0.label: Hatschbourg (Hattstatt & Vœgtlinshoffen, 47.36 ha)
3.items.0.desc: Marl-limestone plus loess deposits, thick and well-drained. Medieval records; prices were high in the 16th–17th centuries. Mainly Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris and Riesling, with Muscat showing fine flavour. The wines have outstanding typicity, fully developed aromas and strong ageing ability.
3.items.1.label: Hengst (Wintzenheim, 75.78 ha)
3.items.1.desc: Oligocene conglomerate plus calcareous marl; "Hengst" means "stallion". Recorded in a 9th-century donation to Murbach abbey. Mainly Gewurztraminer, showing "wildness" when young and, after 10–20 years or more in bottle, becoming a refined "thoroughbred".
3.items.2.label: Kirchberg de Barr (Barr, 40.63 ha)
3.items.2.desc: Limestone to marl-limestone, rich in Middle Jurassic limestone-block gravel with Tertiary conglomerate cover. Named for the Saint-Martin chapel at the top of the hill, and already prized in 1760. Gewurztraminer, Riesling and Pinot Gris are all fine; they ripen later but show astonishing structure and spice with age.
4.question: The site name Hengst (Wintzenheim), "stallion", reflects what stylistic evolution of its wines?
4.options.0: Very tame and elegant from youth, with no change at all
4.options.1: Shows a "wild" character when young and is tamed into a refined "thoroughbred" only after 10–20 years or more in bottle
4.options.2: Shows its style only in certain vintages
4.options.3: Not suited to ageing at all and must be drunk early
4.explanation: Hengst means "stallion", a name that aptly describes the stylistic evolution of the Gewurztraminer here: in youth it shows a rough, "wild" character, and needs a long period (10–20 years or more) of bottle ageing to be tamed, becoming soft and refined and finally showing striking elegance — just as taming a thoroughbred takes time and patience.
5.keyPoints.0: Marl-limestone is the largest of the ten families, with 13 Grand Crus; this lesson covers the first 7
5.keyPoints.1: Eichberg (57.62 ha): the lowest-rainfall area around Colmar, extremely rich Gewurztraminer
5.keyPoints.2: Goldert: named for "gold", given priority selling by the Lucerne city council in 1728
5.keyPoints.3: Hengst (75.78 ha): the "stallion" name, wild when young and elegant after long ageing
5.keyPoints.4: Kirchberg de Barr: named for the Saint-Martin chapel at the top of the hill, prized as early as 1760
